finding_key: packages/documentation/sheets/datasources.md::new docs page misstates the datasource access model: collaborators can execute queries with the owner's stored credentials
evidence: The new page's "Good to know" bullet (datasources.md, last section) says the connection "belongs to the person who created it" and that collaborators "run their own connection to execute it", implying the creator's credentials are private to them. The supplied backend code contradicts that: `POST datasources/:id/query` in datasource.controller.ts only does `findRaw` + `workspaceService.assertMember(ds.workspaceId, userId)` (no author/role check — assertMember accepts any membership row regardless of role), and `DataSourceService.executeQuery` builds the client via `createClient(ds)` with `decrypt(ds.password)`, i.e. the creator's stored credentials. So any workspace member can run arbitrary validated SELECTs against the creator's PostgreSQL instance, which is the opposite of the documented model. I could not inspect the frontend datasource-view UI (not supplied), but the API-level behaviour is definitive for the doc's assertion; the defect is documentation-only, hence major rather than critical.
